posts.name: Urukeli
posts.cooked:
Key Takeaways

Every MCP tool now takes a studio_id, so agents address Studios explicitly instead of relying on session state. Multi-Studio, multi-client workflows are more reliable, clients pick up the change automatically, Assistant Settings shows connected AI clients, and we fixed two stability issues.

Hi Creators,

We’re making a round of updates to the Studio MCP Server that lets you connect MCP-enabled AI agents to Studio and make changes directly to Studio sessions.

Multi-Agent Improvements

Before this release, an MCP client was bound to a single Studio instance through the set_active_studio tool. If several agents shared a single MCP connection, they couldn’t reliably address different Studios.

Routing is now explicit. Each tool call must specify the Studio it targets instead of relying on session state. This matches how stateless MCP servers are meant to work, and it makes workflows with multiple Studio instances and multiple clients more reliable.

To get this update, restart your AI client once after Studio updates itself. From there, clients like Claude Code and Codex pick up the new tools on their own.

Key updates in this version include:

  • studio_id on every tool call: Each call names the Studio instance it targets. set_active_studio is removed, so if you were calling it directly, pass studio_id instead.
  • Place ID in list_roblox_studios: The tool call also returns the Place ID alongside its name and Studio instance ID, with the exception of local places that don’t have one, so those are still listed by name only. The Place ID lets an agent pick the right Studio when two open Studios share a name, to further improve multi-agent support.

Connected AI Clients

Assistant Settings now shows which AI clients are connected to the Studio MCP Server. Hover the tooltip on the MCP Servers page to see the list. If an agent isn’t responding, check here to confirm its MCP connection is live.

image11664×1240 356 KB

View connected clients from Assistant Settings > MCP Servers

Other Improvements

We also fixed two stability issues:

  • Fixed the MCP Server returning “method not implemented” for valid tool calls, which happened when parts of the server lost connection to each other. Those calls now resolve correctly.
  • Fixed the MCP Server disabling itself. Several people reported the setting turning off on its own, which meant no Studio instances showed up when their AI client listed them.

What’s Next

We’ll be making regular improvements to the Studio MCP Server in the coming months. We also plan to add more structured data like Universe ID to list_roblox_studios entries, so agents can identify the right Studio to run tools against.

If you’re running several agents or clients against multiple Studio instances over MCP, let us know how the studio_id change works for you.

Happy creating!

The Roblox Studio Team

About crashes - it is unfortunate. We are trying to fix them all, and if you have some way to reproduce them it makes our job much easier.
